verdict.rationale: Basecamp documents its own Card Tables, which are kanban boards it explicitly positions for software development and bug/issue tracking. They are backed by assignable to-dos with due dates and Hill Charts for progress, so agile-style work can be planned and tracked. However, there is no documented sprint or iteration concept (time-boxed cycles, sprint backlog, sprint scope), so sprint management itself rests on the user arranging these pieces. Missing for 10: native time-boxed sprints/iterations, backlog and sprint planning, velocity/burndown or story-point estimation, and independent corroboration of agile sprint use.

support.subject: As an engineer, I can plan and manage sprints for agile software development

citations.quote: Card Tables are our take on kanban boards. Add cards, set up columns, and move work through phases.
Perfect for bug and issue tracking, software development, production work, or anything with distinct stages.
Assign items, set due dates, attach files, even create subtasks.
Basecamp’s Hill Charts let you know exactly where things really stand.
